source.stem:
The graph represents the motion of a train travelling between two stations.
0 100 200 300 400 500 600 700 800 900 Which statement about the train is correct?

options.text: Its acceleration takes a longer time than its deceleration.
It travels at constant speed for less than half of its journey time.
It travels 2000 m in the first 100 s.
It travels 10⁰⁰0 m at constant speed.

intelligence.enrichment: Speed equals total distance covered divided by total time taken; metre/second is written as m/s and kilometre/hour is written as km/h. Dividing distance by time gives distance per unit time, and the distance and time units determine the speed unit. The learner correctly applies this rule: Speed equals total distance covered divided by total time taken; metre/second is written as m/s and kilometre/hour is written as km/h. Speed can be found by dividing the two numbers in either order and copying a familiar unit from the question.
